subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw implement artifact-gated status updates and no-idle-after-green as core runtime policy, and if so should the remaining work extend the current run-lifecycle/diagnostic state instead of adding a separate run-state file and ENFORCEMENT_GUARDS_V1 flag?
rationale: The desired reliability outcome fits the stability roadmap, but the requested mechanism adds new runtime policy, persisted state, status-message blocking, and a feature flag; automation should not choose those product and compatibility defaults without maintainer intent.

options.title: Stage On Existing Runtime State
options.body: Adopt only the remaining artifact/status and post-green invariants, implemented through existing reply-run activity, diagnostics, and SQLite-owned state rather than a parallel file/flag system.

options.title: Close As Covered By Run Lifecycle Work
options.body: Treat PR 102160 and the closed run-lifecycle umbrella as sufficient, accepting that exact artifact-gated status and post-green idle semantics will not be tracked here.

options.title: Keep As Broad Umbrella
options.body: Leave this issue open as a product umbrella until maintainers split explicit sub-issues for status gating, persistence, timers, telemetry, and completion enforcement.

recommendation.title: Stage On Existing Runtime State
recommendation.body: Adopt only the remaining artifact/status and post-green invariants, implemented through existing reply-run activity, diagnostics, and SQLite-owned state rather than a parallel file/flag system.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus owned the overlapping run-lifecycle design and PR stack, making them the best available owner for deciding whether these remaining guardrails belong in that architecture.
